The Vortex flow meters have as basic principle the Vortex accomplishment around obstacles that are placed against the fluid flow. The resulting vibrations are converted into electrical signal through using, in general, piezoelectric sensors. Vortex flowmeters are designed for measuring and counting with high precision liquid flow rates at high speeds and low viscosity. Coanda flowmeters based on the “Coanda effect”, physical phenomenon showing that a free jet of fluid which occurs in a nozzles or pipes, tends to track the nearest surface, attached to it. The experimental study was done on the structure of a flowmeter with “Coanda effect” and acceleration transducer, which transforms frequency oscillations in electrical signal proportional to the amount of liquid flow.

articleTitle: Simulation and PLC control of an electromechanical actuator with volatile liquid
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents the study and operating control of an electromechanical actuator with volatile liquid (EAVL). The paper proposes a practical approach for EAVL displacement control using a PLC technology and a linear potentiometer transducer. Proposed electromechanical actuator has two essential features: low linear displacement and high strength. The electromechanical actuator is a technical dynamic system that can be investigated through transfer functions. In this regard, the step response of the EAVL was analyzed, the transfer functions (experimental and theoretical) and time constants values were identified for different quantities of volatile liquid used inside of actuator. Through transfer functions were analyzed parameters characterizing the dynamic properties of the system: delay, transient regime speed, response time and the coefficient of amplification. Also, the results of the evaluation through finite element method are analyzed. The EAVL behavior on the temperature and pressure variation is presented.

articleTitle: Sliding mode control for efficient utilization of renewable energy sources in DC micro grid: A comparison with a linear PID controller
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: With the advances in the manufacturing of photo voltaic cells, Dc-Dc micro grids are gaining a lot of attention. With the concept of parallel operation of different Dc energy sources like photo voltaic cells, fuel cells, storage banks like super capacitors and different type of batteries has evolved the structure of Dc micro grids. To get benefit from the concept of dc micro grids, the problem of circulating currents among parallel energy sources must be solved. Due to very low resistance of dc micro grids, a voltage difference of few millivolts between two energy sources may cause one source to operate at full load while the other being idle. This research paper proposes a sliding mode control to solve the problem of circulating currents and unbalanced load sharing. A comparison of SM control with PID control is also presented.

articleTitle: A fuzzy hybrid approach for reliability optimization problem in power distribution systems
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Reliability optimization in power distribution systems is obviously an important problem. The power distribution system supplies electricity to their consumers maintaining economy as a well as reliability. In this paper, an algorithm intending for cost minimization in electrical distribution systems is proposed. Combing two well-known meta-heuristic algorithms namely Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Quantum behaved Particle Swarm Optimization (QPSO), an efficient and noble hybrid algorithm has been introduced in this article. For the input variables (cost, weight and volume), fuzzy models with triangular membership functions are used. The results of the proposed approach were compared with those from other exiting approaches, showing that the outcomes from our approach are more acceptable than others.

articleTitle: Power control and energy management of a Lebanese smart micro grid
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper, an energy management algorithm of a micro grid used in the Lebanese cases is presented. The proposed microgrid is supplying a residential load and is composed of renewable and non renewable energy sources. The renewable energy sources are PV and wind turbine. The model and simulation results of the PV and the wind turbine systems with a Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) controller is presented, with a controller based on the perturb and observe algorithm for the PV and a fuzzy logic controller for the wind turbine. The model and simulation results of the PV/Wind hybrid system with a storage system is also treated. This hybrid system is coupled to the non renewable energy sources through an inverter and a transformer. These sources are the Lebanese grid and a backup diesel generator. The control of the inverter is discussed in this paper for the on-grid and off-grid cases. An energy management algorithm is finally proposed and validated.

articleTitle: Predefined recovery exercises system for after stroke hand rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents the design of an intelligent haptic robotic glove (IHRG) model for the rehabilitation of the patients that have been diagnosed with a cerebrovascular accident (CVA). Total loss or loss of range of motion, decreased reaction times and disordered movement organization create deficits in motor control, which affect the patient's independent living. The proposed approach aims to improve the recovery programs using a set of predefined rehabilitation exercises. They will work together and, according to the hand movement, the progress will be encountered when the patient uses more his own force and less the controlled glove. The final goal was the integration of the haptic robotic glove with Shadow Dexterous Hand and ROS (Robot Operating System). In this way the glove movements made by a patient wearing it, will be found in the virtual reality simulator.

articleTitle: Java technology used to facilitate measuring activity performed by students in laboratory
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Taking in consideration the new trends in Open Source Systems, we present a solution based Java technology used to help students to take measurements in the lab. Also it can be integrated as an educational remote laboratory. The remote laboratory consist in a web server, where students can access to educational materials and also collect data from different stands having the possibility to also control them, under a supervised and controlled environment. The stands are made with industrial devices: programmable logic controller (PLC), human machine interface (HMI) and various industrial sensors. This system can be very useful in the new information society to create a modern virtual laboratory for a remote teaching.

articleTitle: Simulation of some dynamic regimes specific to permanent-magnet motors used for electrical motor-scooters
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents a series of dynamic regimes specific to the operation of permanent-magnet synchronous motors used for electrical motor-scooters. On this purpose, there is presented the mathematical model of the motor. By means of this model, there has been carried out a programs package of simulation (in Matlab); a part of these simulations are presented in this paper. There have been considered three particular situations: dynamic processes in the absence of the permanent magnet and weak damping, dynamic processes in the absence of the permanent magnet and strong damping and dynamic processes in the presence of the permanent magnet. The paper ends by conclusions obtained from the simulations analysis.

articleTitle: Study on the influence of wireless communication technology on infusion pumps
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In previous studies our concern was the electromagnetic compatibility in terms of life-supporting medical equipment in intensive care units. Following the results obtained, we decided to intensify our efforts in the field of electromagnetic compatibility trials of medical devices, including raising awareness of the problems of electromagnetic interference. In this work we have studied the influence of the electromagnetic field on infusion pumps / injectomats equipment used in all health facilities, not only intensive care. A very important aspect in this study is that these types of equipment used in administering medication are found in ambulances for example, a medium in which the electromagnetic field is very strong.

articleTitle: The problems of dissolved in oil gases analysis results' interpretation in information analytical systems
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The power transformers state analysis based on different DGA approaches is presented in the paper. The DGA results interpretation complexity in modern information analytical systems of the high voltage equipment technical state assessment was revealed. The necessity of information analytical systems training and self-training principles was justified. Applying these principles for new data and formalized expert knowledge extraction will improve estimates quality.

articleTitle: Comparative measurements on an electronic weighing instrument
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Many times was heard the dilemma: “To measure or not to measure, that is the question”. But, when you measure, a question arises: how accurate/reliable are your measurements results so that the client should have the confidence that you measure in the right way? No matter how carefully you perform internal checks, systematic errors often can go unnoticed. For this reason, the simplest way to check the quality of your measurements is to participate in proficiency testing scheme (PTS) / interlaboratory comparison (ILC). Moreover, ISO/IEC 17025 requires “that laboratories have quality control procedures for monitoring the validity of tests and calibrations undertaken”. It is therefore important that you should regularly compare your measurement results with those of other laboratories so, to attend in intercomparisons. In this way, this paper describes and analyzes the comparative results and uncertainties associated obtained by a reference laboratory and other six participating laboratories, appearing with codes that have been assigned during the comparison. The proficiency test item consisted in a NAWI (non-automatic weighing instrument) having Max 6 kg and resolution of 10 mg. The measurements were performed at Mass laboratory of INM which was designated as Pilot (LP) and Reference Laboratory (LR). The determinations began in March 2015 and concluded in August 2015. The goal of interlaboratory comparison was to provide verification of each participating laboratory's measurement capability by obtaining a measurement that agrees with the LP/LR. The results are analyzed using En (normalized errors) values.

articleTitle: Geometry influence on the precision of light flux measurement with ulbricht integrating sphere
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Integrating sphere is a device that canhave important structural dimensions and weight, generating the possibility for somedeformations to occur. In general, the measurement chains are used with the analysis of the sources of errors, but no information was found about the errors generated by the integrating sphere itself. Geometric errors caused by imperfections could generate systematic errors, even immediately after sphere calibration with a standard source of light. The phenomenon of multiple reflections on a surface which is not spherical will induce errors that depend on the lighting distribution of the measured luminaire and his mounting position. The paper examines these assumptions to estimate the scale of the geometric imperfections (constructive or created in time) in correlation with the errors introduced in the measured luminous flux. Original MAT LAB functions and DIALux are used to evaluate the light reflection between surfaces.

articleTitle: A new mathematical model for the command sequence generator of a two-phase hybrid stepper motor
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Modeling processes before physical experimenting is a necessary a preliminary stage for verification and validation of a proposed algorithm of command and control. Elaborating of these algorithms for microcontrollers through a written code, compiled and uploaded into memory consumes valuable time. Reducing this spent time can be obtained through special developed compilers for different types of microcontrollers in Matlab®-Simulink®. In this paper are presented new mathematical models which describe the command sequences of a stepper motor. These mathematical models are simulated within the Matlab-Simulink software and validated through an Arduino Uno development board (with Atmel microcontroller). The obtained results through software modeling are confirmed by experimental results.

articleTitle: Aspects regarding the nonintrusive load monitoring and electrical equipment diagnosis from power substations
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The nonintrusive load monitoring is an emerging technology which aims to control energy consumption and the analysis of electrical equipment behavior from power substation internal services equipment. The paper describes a calculus method and a system for nonintrusive load monitoring of the electrical parameters from the auxiliary services on a power substation.

articleTitle: Survey on the efficiency and the profitability of an hybrid wind/PV system: The Lebanese case
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper, the study treats the energy production from renewable sources, especially from solar PV and wind turbine. The experimental results, obtained from each source alone and from a hybrid system installed in Lebanon, are analyzed and compared. Economical study of these separated systems and for the hybrid system are given. The profitability of the different sources, separately or jointly in one hybrid system, is analyzed for a period equal to their life time.

articleTitle: The magnetic field of asynchronous machines with concentrated winding
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper is devoted to the analysis of concentrated windings, which are lately used in electric machines of alternative current. Processes for suppressing the 5 and 7 order harmonics are indicated for improving the deformed shape of magnetic induction curve of the air gap. The magnetic induction curve of air gap was estimated by applying the finite element method form and the values of the flux and magnetic induction were presented. The stray magnetic fluxes of frontal parts of concentrated winding had been determined by concomitantly applying the indicated method. The obtained results confirmed that the concentrated windings used in electromechanical converters of alternative current reduce the quantity of copper used in the front parts by approximately 25%.

articleTitle: Temperature intelligent control based on soft computing technology
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents an intelligent method based of soft computing to control thermal processes. A fuzzy logic controller (FLC) is designed to control the temperature of an electric oven. The temperature control is based on a fuzzy learning algorithm with auto-tuning capabilities in order to get as performances, time response as short as possible, small overshoot and zero steady state error. The auto-tuning FLC is implemented in LabVIEW software from National Instruments. The experimental results clearly emphasize the capabilities of the proposed FLC to realize the best performances.

articleTitle: Study on voltage dynamics in power grids with renewable energy sources integration
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents an analysis of voltage dynamics for a test system, considering or not renewable sources integration in the electricity grid. The analysis was carried out for the n-1 contingency criterion. The simulations were conducted using PowerFactory DigSilent software and the New England 39-bus test system.

articleTitle: Fluid model used for simulating streamer breakdown in SF6 and SF6-N2 mixtures
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The algorithm for flux limiting technique is used in the present research. The experiments have been implemented using a high frequency sinusoidal voltage superimposed to a steep fronted voltage step.

articleTitle: Screen-printed Pb(Mg, Nb)O3-PbTiO3 thick tilms on ceramic substrates for sensor applications
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this work the screen-printed piezoelectric 0.65Pb(Mg<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/3</sub>Nb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2/3</sub>)O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-0.35PbTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> thick films were prepared on metalized low-temperature co-fired ceramic substrates. Such substrates are interesting for micro-electro mechanical systems, for example for piezoelectric sensors and actuators. The prepared thick films exhibit the piezoelectric coefficient d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">33</sub> equal to 120 pC/N.

articleTitle: Transient analysis of wound rotor synchronous motor synchronisation using finite elements method
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper deals with wound rotor synchronous motor synchronization when the motor starts in asynchronous regime. “The fineness” of the synchronization will be studied in terms of the following parameters: the value of the starting resistance, the value of the DC voltage and the position of the rotor against magnetic field of the stator at the moment when the excitation winding is connected to the DC voltage. The transient analysis was carried out using a program based on finite elements method (FEM).

articleTitle: Fractional slot permanent magnet machine with outer rotor
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper deals with the study of fractional slot permanent magnet synchronous machine, under 9 slots/10 poles structure, with outer rotor. It reports some results obtained by means of FEM-based simulation, which have as main goal the improvement of output characteristics. More specific, the inner diameter of the rotor and the stator shoe shape are modified. The analysis takes into consideration both motoring and generating duty and refer mainly to cogging torque and back emf.

articleTitle: Vibration mini actuator with magnetically suspended inertial mass
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Miniaturization and the need to obtain vibration actuators with increased reliability, having a multitude of practical applications, led to the development of a subset of actuators, namely those with magnetically suspended inertial mass, with absolutely no elastic moving element subjected to mechanical wear. This paper investigates an original model of nonconventional electromagnetic vibrator having an inertial magneto-elastic mass suspended in a ferrofluid. The permanent magnet used as inertial mass is self-levitated in the ferrofluid, and the magnet vibrations are transmitted in exterior through an elastically suspension (inertial vibrator), constituted by the ferrofluid when a sinusoidal current passes through the coil/coils of the device. Such vibrators can be used for cellular phones and haptic systems or active vibration damping.

articleTitle: Characterization of different types of gliding discharges: Electrical parameters and breakdown simulation
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Gliding electric discharges have been intensively used in the last 20 years for practical applications in many fields: gas cleaning, gas reformation, aqueous solutions cleaning, microbiological decontamination, hydrogen production, surface treatment etc. All applications are based on the action of electrochemical active species produced by these discharges in different configurations of electrochemical reactors. Each configuration can favor one or other of the active species. The power supply of the reactors provides a voltage of a few kilovolts and limited values of the electric current, usually less than 1 A. After the initial breakdown of the discharge, a gas flow will elongate it until the energy density per volume unit decreases under the threshold level and the discharge will extinct. In this paper the evolutions of the electrical parameters are analyzed for three different configurations of reactors producing gliding electric discharges. Two of them are completely new. All three used the same power supply. A breakdown simulation of each configuration has been done using the COMSOL Multiphysics software. The analysis and the simulation allow the optimization of the structural parameters for each reactor in order to provide the best interface for active species transfer.

articleTitle: Statistical analysis of LED light flux variations
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Practical installations of illuminance systems use Light Emitting Diodes (LED) more and more. In most of the cases, tests in the field have shown that the details listed on the lights' technical specifications differ from the field values. The present study has been done on 7 W light sources with a 700 lm nominal light flux. We use statistical methods on multiple measurements sets on LEDs to determine the simple and synthetic indicators by which we estimate the homogeneity of the LED sample set and verify the truth of the technical descriptions listed on the packages sold on the market. In various studies on the behavior of LED sources we found significant differences between the values determined luminous fluxes and those listed in the box trading. These findings have led us to conduct tests on larger groups of the same type of LED sources, to see if it complies with the Certificate of Conformity, referring to standard deviation. For the analyzed group it was found that the manufacturer does not comply with this regulation.

articleTitle: Methodological challenges in near-field exposure assessment of personnel operating military radio equipment using personal exposimeters: Possible difficulties in compliance analysis
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this study we report on the relationship between the field strength (both electric and magnetic components) measured by the exposimeter placed in the upper pocket of a group of subjects equipped with a backpacked military radio transceiver (VHF) and the unperturbed field values at the location of the human body/exposimeter position without the human body present. We propose correction factors for the investigated scenarios, for different spatial averaging methods and discuss methodological challenges in near field exposure assessment.

articleTitle: On the assessment of optical power budget in an optical system for detecting of partial discharge in high voltage electrical equipment
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper, the computation algorithm of the attenuation of optical signal duet o the optical power losses, in an optical system for partial discharge detection is presented. Based on the references in the field, the partial discharge detector based on the interferometer Fabry Perot is described. Numerical evaluation of the components of the attenuation and highlighting the influence of the some quantities affecting them is carried out using a Matlab application. The determination of the loss power budget in an optical path is important in assessing the acoustic-optical sensor sensitivity and in choosing adequately the photodetector.

articleTitle: AGC of practical power system using backtracking search optimization algorithm
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper, backtracking search optimization algorithm (BSA) is proposed to solve automatic generation control (AGC) problem to achieve the best steady state and transient performances of power system. A practical two area multisource power system model is developed by considering different generating units (non-reheat, reheat and hydro) with different real time system parameters and non-linear security constraints such as governor dead band (GDB), generation rate constraint (GRC) and time delay (TD). BSA is used to tune the proportional integral derivative (PID) control parameters to improve the AGC performances considering all practical limitations. A new and innovative cost function is formulated considering area control error, stead state error, maximum overshoot, undershoot and number of peaks present in the output waveform with proper weight factors. The performance of the proposed method is compared with real coded genetic algorithm (RCGA) and particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. Simulation results validate the better performance of BSA tuned PID control method compare to other two methods.

articleTitle: Variance of radiometric performances for cool-white and neutral-white LED luminaries
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Correlated color temperature (CCT) affecting feelings must be adequately adjusted according to the change of atmosphere. White light-emitting diode (LED) spectral for solid state lighting should be designed for high luminous efficacy as well as good color rendering index (CRI). In different applications, when warm-white or cool-white LED's are recommended, we are forced to use also dimmers. In this paper, cool-white and warm-white LEDs resulting from phosphor converted blue (PCB) chips with a wavelength peak of 445 nm and 598 nm are experimented. The tests pursued the radiometric parameters as correlated color temperature, color rendering (Ra) and chromaticity coordinates (x, y) while varying the parameters of the power supply for cool-white LED XPE-CREE 6500 and neutral-white LED XPL4000.

articleTitle: Considerations regarding the practical implementation of the heliothermic actuator in the form of flat spiral spring
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper is presented the authors concern regarding the development of solutions in the field of heliothermic actuators achieved based on the solid heat medium. One of the research directions has led to an actuator with bimetallic band in the form of flat spiral spring and heat conductive fins. In the end of the paper are presented main conclusions regarding the tests made on the actuator with the bimetallic band immersed in various mediums.

articleTitle: A neuro-fuzzy algorithm for middle-term load forecasting
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The forecasting method presented in this paper is intended for industrial customers who mainly have two types of consumers in the distribution grid: consumers for climate control and consumers from production activities. Forecasting model is divided into two subsystems:1. Consumption forecasting using a neural network with back-propagation and using data from previous months and 2. Forecast adjustment using temperature and production load differences for air conditioning and production consumption between the previous months and months for which the forecasting is done.

articleTitle: A brain-computer interface for the control of a finger rehabilitation glove
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper proposes the use of a rehabilitation device that combines a brain-computer interface with a hand exerciser composed of a finger rehabilitation glove. Relevant design strategy of the mechanical structure are submitted, as well as key points of the brain signals decoding algorithms. This setup has the potential to enhance hands gasp function rehabilitation for the II-V fingers. The paper concludes with the formulation of further research direction that are worth to be explored.

articleTitle: Real-time eye movement detection analysis: Comparison between image based algorithm and electrooculogram
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this work we investigate an image based algorithm as a reliablemethod to perceive the eye movement and offer new possibilities for the activity recognition. In order to test the effectiveness of the algorithm, the eye movement data was recorded using an electrooculography system. Different patterns of eye movement were analyzed within the conducted study. Three different lighting and three activities were performed in order to evaluate the performance of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Knowledge-based decisions in smart grids
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper addresses the issue of information management and knowledge-based decisions which are paramount for an efficient operation of smart grids. The ever-growing presence of new technologies, which are supporting novel operation strategies for users and utilities is investigated, based on data provided by real-life electrical power systems actors. Thus, consumption curves from a large customer were used, along with generation profiles for photovoltaic (PV), wind generation and electrode-boiler sources. The smart generation environment assessment will then be performed by taking into account various generation and consumption characteristics, designed to cover the majority of cases. The paper addressed the impact of distributed generation on both distribution systems operation and energy management systems.

articleTitle: Interactive system for optimizing the operation of a transformer with continuously adjustable voltage
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper aims to achieve an optimized system for cooling the sliding contact used at the commutation of the transformers with continuously adjustable voltage using an Arduino microcontroller board and to analyze the efficiency of various cooling systems for an economical and secure exploitation of these equipment.

articleTitle: The recovery of the postural equilibrium by balancing the baric pressure at the level of the lower limbs for patients who had a stroke by using the MBT device
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The cerebral vascular diseases are a major issue of public health, being on the second place in Europe after the cardiovascular diseases. The rehabilitation of the patients diagnosed with a stroke requires long-term programmes of recovery and healthcare, which determines increased costs of the medical recovery for the patients as well as for the society. Even though the recovery methods after the stroke are customized according to each patient, the purpose is the same: to gain a functional status that could allow independence, the physical and psychical adaptation to the changes determined by the stroke as well as the integration into the family and society.

articleTitle: Interconnection of medical data acquisition systems
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents a system which interconnects the Hospital Information Systems (HIS) implemented on different medical institutions and makes possible the data transfer between hospitals. The system integrates a middleware cloud component which ensures protection against external and especially, internal data leakage attacks. Also, the system implements a “plug&play” principle which makes it very flexible in the process of adding new data sources.

articleTitle: Cardiac arrhythmia classification using T-complexity measure
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper we propose to investigate the possibility to use the randomness from different types of arrhythmias for detection and classification of them from ECG signals. Randomness present in discrete time series is strongly connected with complexity of information present in substrings associated with time series and an appropriate coding of the RR interval associated with a complexity measure can give themselves the enough data for a good classification of arrhythmia. In this paper we propose to use the values given by T-complexity applied to RR intervals and a binary classification tree for 13 classes of arrhythmias with satisfactory results.

articleTitle: Students course “introduction to industrial image recognition”
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In part I of this paper a brief overview about state-of-the-art industrial image processing is given. Part II shows how an introduction of this technology can be taught to newcomers in the field, how problems can be solved using image recognition and processing systems and how this can be achieved with good success within very short teaching time by means of a step-by-step example.

articleTitle: The study of possibility to use the current transformer for power conversion
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The current transformer is largely used in power system as instrument transformer which made possible the measurement of big intensity current (hundreds or thousands of Amps) by reducing to accessible values for usual instruments (1-5 amperes). Nominal current ratio and accuracy class characterizes it. Current transformer can supply measurement instruments connected to secondary winding, nominal power being in the range 10-102 VA. Exceeding of nominal power has as result exceeding of operating errors allowed by accuracy class. Use of current transformer for power transfer between primary and secondary windings, not as measurement instrument represents the main aim of the paper. Its design in that purpose will be made beginning from technique and economic reasons (nominal power, material consumption, power looses, efficiency etc.). It takes in consideration that secondary power has to be a constant voltage independent of primary current value for a large range of its variation (20...120% from nominal current). There are presented also the experimental results made on current transformers used in power system or in laboratory, with magnetic core made by laminated silica steel or permalloy. There are verified practically dimensioning relations obtained for current transformer used as power converter and power transfer.

articleTitle: The effect of gas and solution flow rate on nitrates and H2O2 generation in NTP discharges
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The effects flow rates of gas, liquid, or gas composition, in non-thermal plasma (NTP) electrical discharge reactors, on nitrates and hydrogen peroxide generation in water, have been studied. The reactor set up consists of two stainless steel tubes placed in a glass tube. The effects of successive passing the same sample water through one, two or three identical columns of NTP electrical discharge, were determined by serial connection of several similar reactors (up to three). In all cases, the efficiency of the nitrates and hydrogen peroxide production in treated water in the NTP reactor(s) have been also calculated.

articleTitle: A hybrid GA-PSO algorithm for static VAR compensation
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Static VAR compensation is used as a fast response mechanism for dynamic voltage regulation in transmission grids. SVCs use electronically controlled shunt capacitors and reactors to inject or draw reactive power from the grid. This paper investigates the performance of standard Particle Swarm Optimization and Genetic Algorithms and proposes a hybrid GA-PSO approach for choosing the optimal buses for SVC devices placement in an electrical transmission network, with the objective of voltage regulation in steady operating state.

articleTitle: Overcurrent protection using a new type of electric fuse
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The electric fuses are one of the very well-known protection electrical apparatus which are used for domestic and especially in industrial applications. They have many advantages in comparison with other protection electrical apparatus as small overall dimensions, fast acting and small costs. Form protection point of view they isolate the load from the main source of power. Due to the fact that time of clearing fault current is the main parameter, in order to transform the time-current characteristic into an adjustable one, it has been developed the concept of controlled fusing. In this paper, the principle of controlled fusing applied to high breaking capacity fuses, is described. The protection of electronic devices, especially for power semiconductors, using the proposed controlled fuse, can be extended to other critical parameters from the protected electrical installation.

articleTitle: Vibro-acoustic behavior vs. conductive interferences in PMSM drives
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper, a simplified high frequency model of the Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) as well as the motor drive were developed and analyzed using Simulink. The currents in the normal and common mode paths were extracted and compared with the analytical results. A Finite Element Analysis (FEA) was performed on two PMSM with different topologies in order to obtain the radial forces on the stator teeth. The results were analyzed in order to try to establish a link between said forces and the high-frequency emissions that are present in the system.

articleTitle: Non-contact heart rate estimation from a video sequence
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Heart rate (HR) is a biomedical parameter, which contains information about the autonomic nervous system activity, and thus, it can predict health related events. Non — contact acquisition of the HR can be of interest not only for clinical practice situations but also for more commercial oriented usage. In this paper, the estimation of HR from a video sequence acquired with a smartphone camera (non — contact recording method) is evaluated. The validation is realized using the HR estimated from an ECG signal via contact electrodes. A reliable HR is obtained from the video sequence, making the method suitable for applications like low cost driver fatigue detection systems.

articleTitle: Overview on energy efficiency parameters in data centres
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper proposes alternatives of energy efficiency assessment for data centres. Data centres are the core of present information and communication economy. Since the early days of telecom's facilities, the operators' main challenges were the equipment placement, capacity planning, expansion, redundancy and availability of services, all these factors leading to power consumption inefficiencies. The evolution of Information and Communication Technology (ICT or IT&C) and cloud computing, increase the storage and processing capacity conduct to an exponential growth of Information Technology (IT) resources that have to be hosted and provide continuing operation. Beside of availability factor, the optimal utilization of the capacity and energy efficiency are the main characteristics of Data Centre facility. The overall efficiency of a data centre has to be precisely calculated to establish parameters of comparison, estimate environmental impact and to decide the specific measures for reducing energy consumption. The practical design, simulation and measurement have made it possible a comparison of efficiency parameters regarding energy consumption and IT utilization density.

articleTitle: Distributed processing of data streams on the edge devices
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Diversity of communication technologies in Internet of Things and increasing the amount of sensor data outlined the idea of using intermediate devices for storage and pre-processing - such as gateways in sensor networks. Moreover, semantic interoperability is emerging as an attractive solution for communication between autonomous entities or smart objects in Internet of Things, so the paper examines the functionalities of semantic data annotation in embedded devices with limited resources located at the edge of the Smart Grid network.

articleTitle: Electrochemical techniques used to characterize electrochemical cells
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper, we present some techniques used to characterize the electrochemical cells. The main role of the batteries is to provide power and to recharge using DC. The research led to the identification of different charging methods which prevent battery damage. Conventional processes are highlighted and some of them provide the opportunity to stimulate battery electrodes and thus, prevent battery damage. In this regard, the most effective methods are processes using current pulses during charging and discharging.

articleTitle: Analysis of low power asynchronous motors operation at variable voltages and frequencies
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The electromechanical conversion is a very important aspect in the conversion process of the energy; it is carried out by means of the electrical machines used in all areas of the human activity. By using the electronic computer in the electrical machines design, there can be obtained some better operation characteristics, there can be decreased the losses of electrical energy and increased the power factor. The computer-aided conception becomes a numerical laboratory, where the prototypes are built and tested. Improving the design quality cannot neglect the saturation in case of machines strictly dimensioned from electrical and magnetic point of view. Developing some performant electrical drives with high response speed and exploring closer and closer by the stability limit of the asynchronous motors have led to intense preoccupations, both in our country and abroad, for determining the parameters precisely. The research carried out proves that the low speed operation means an increase of the machine losses, by 18.2% and a low decrease of the reactive power consumption, by 5.1%.

articleTitle: Fire behavior analysis for new retardant nanocomposite formulations with minimum risk to health and safety
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper are presented new retardant nanocomposite formulations with minimum risk to health and safety.

articleTitle: A two layer ground computational model for the numerical simulations of the earthing systems
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: A two layer ground model for the computation of the earthing systems is presented. The model combines the pipe element method with multiple image technique by using a fundamental solution defined for the two-layered three-dimensional (3D) half space. The model couples two problems: an external one that models the phenomena that occur in the soil - solved with the boundary element method (BEM), and an internal one that models the potential distribution in the buried metallic structures - solved with the finite element method (FEM). In order to evaluate the two layer ground computational model, the resistance-to-earth is computed for three particular earthing systems (vertical rod, horizontal rod and gradient control mat) and compared with the analytical solution. The earth potential rise (EPR) in case of the gradient control mat is represented.

articleTitle: Low-speed sensorless field-oriented control of asynchronous machine based on adaptive flux error suppression method
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper, the sensorless field-oriented control of asynchronous machine with squirrel-cage rotor (AMS) at the low-speed operation will be observed. The identification of rotor speed from adaptive flux error as well as the adaptation mechanism will be investigated. At first, the background of model reference adaptive system (MRAS) will be revised. Later, the mathematical model of AMS in the stationary reference frame will be presented for decoupling of flux term. After that, the adaptive scheme based on relevant flux terms will be presented. One as a reference model and one another as an adaptive model. Finally, the simulation result based on defined parameters will be discussed.

articleTitle: Comparative study of gas sensing microsensors based on sulfonated CNTs and CNTs/Polyaniline mixture
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Two gas microsensors, based on SWCNT, were obtained and used for different gases detection, like CO, NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. On an interdigitized gold electrode structure were deposited, as active layers, sulfonated carbon nanotubes (s-CNTs) and carbon nanotubes (CNTs)/Polyaniline (PANi) mixture, respectively. In order to obtain sulfonated CNT, the available CNTs were activated in a sulfuric acid solution, under different temperatures gradients ranging from 60°C to 300°C. With the obtained microsensors based on sulfonated CNTs, the response and recovery time where investigated and the results are presented and compared. In the case of carbon nanotubes (CNTs)/Polyaniline (PANi) mixture the electrical conductivity of PANi in the deposited layer could be orders of magnitude boosted by controlled doping of polyaniline level in the relative carbon concentration. The obtained microsensors presents improved electrochemical activity and stability in their structure. An efficient low-powered sensor-system based on the presented microsensors represent a viable solution for possible practical application in the field of environmental monitoring, automation, nuclear industry, industrial process control, etc.

articleTitle: Automated system for optimising the production of compressed air with a compressors station
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper we present a solution to save electrical components and energy in a system that produces compressed air. This system has a couple of compressors and when are connected to one tank these compressors work unsynchronized. Our solution reduces the number of start-ups for each one and minimalizes the cost of maintenance.

articleTitle: Induced fault current simulation of a three phase miniature circuit breaker: Simulation of fault and comparison to tripping curve of the MCB
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents the computer aided design (CAD) and computer aided engineering (CAE) modeling of a 3 phase Circuit Breaker in order to analyze the electromagnetic field (EMF) distribution, and the induced current generated by a fault in one of the three phases. In a first step the detailed three dimensional (3D) CAD model of the circuit breaker is created in the CAD environment PTC Creo Elements v.18.1. Then, the exact 3D model is imported in the Ansoft Maxwell v. 15 CAE environment and the electromagnetic field distribution and induced current are computed. The fields along the axis trough the coils are compared to the catalog tripping characteristic of a 3 phase MCB.

articleTitle: Root-cause analysis of cascaded ground faults on an ungrounded distributed network
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This article presents a root cause analysis of a plant trip due to an intermittent ground fault in an ungrounded network. Damages were caused on motor termination boxes due to High Voltage flash over. It appears that specifications supplied by network operator are not in compliance with the issues we observed. Therefore improvements in the network upstream are required and a possibility of a dedicated supply and therefore a conversion into a high resistance grounded systems will be investigated. Installation of suitable surge arresters on the incomer is also something that will be considered.

articleTitle: Resonant inverter with All Digital PLL control
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In many cases, control system of the resonant inverter is on the basis of the PLL algorithm. Widely used analogues specialized integral circuit can not connect directly to the digital modules of inverter control system. Once defined the parameters of the analog PLL by values of R and C, they can not be changed during the working process. Using All-Digital PLL each input and output parameter has digital format and easy can be changed with very good accuracy and read/write by the main control system controller in dynamic operating mode. Main attention in the article is paid to the principle and design of All-Digital PLL control system for the resonant inverter programmed in complex programmable logic device CoolRinner2 (XILINX).

articleTitle: Automation with MFD Titan for lighting control
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents the use of a Moeller MFD Titan in the automation of an indoor lighting installation: energy is saved by using lamps with electronic ballast that allows control through analog inputs. The purpose of the automation is to regulate the light level in the room according to a setting value imposed by the user, taking into count the level given by an illuminance sensor with analog output and a passive infrared sensor (PIR sensor). In order to have full control over the application, a manual mode is created wherein the user can set the power level of the lamps directly. For an optimal control of the lighting, the use of a PID module is required, the latter achieving the hysteresis between the times of the lamp's turning on and off. By using the illuminance sensors and the passive infrared sensor, PIR, the system succeeds in both saving energy and in correcting the errors caused by forgetting the lights on or turning it on during the day when it is not necessary.

articleTitle: Isolux curves on the diffuse reflectance of light on concave dihedral angle
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Understanding the lighting distribution is very important even today, when there are available some simulation software. Building a solution for a lighting system, impose to start from an elaborated initial solution, and at every step it is necessary the interpretation of the results. The main hypothesis of the paper consists in the possibility that some errors could be present in these simulations software, due to the estimation method. This paper analyses the particular case of the dihedral angle between planes, where the inter reflections generates a particular shape for isolux curves. These reflections generate a kind of continuity for illuminance, but only for concave dihedral angle between planes. Starting from DIALux simulations, where the problem was found, authors were using some original MATLAB functions and some comparisons are made, in order to validate the simulations and understanding the lighting configurations. The conclusions are useful for particular simulations, when local reflections described by isolux curves must be interpreted.

articleTitle: The dynamic behavior of electromagnetic plunger drivers for electrical apparatusses with contacts
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents a numerical model for electromagnetic plunger drivers commonly used for electrical commutation apparatuses (EAC) described as electromechanical systems (a mechanism driven by an electromagnet). Starting from energy conservation equations applied to the electromechanical assembly on can define the differential equations system, which mathematical describe the EAC dynamic regime. Due to the fact that the non-linear differential equations system has not analytical solutions, the system must be integrated using a numerical method. The mathematical system is formally the same for the connecting/disconecting regime of EAC, and permits to emphasize the influence of diverse parameters on the transient process of the electromechanical system. Finally, is possible to control and optimize the factors of interest for the circuit commutation (connecting and disconnecting time, contact speed and electromagnetic plunger parameters especially for the ultrafast switchers). In order to sustain the mathematical model, the differential equations have been written for a DC switcher and the data obtained from the numerical calculus had been compared with the experimental data.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic power plant on the ENERED research platform of the electrical engineering faculty of Iasi
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The solar energy is no longer a promise, but a certainty, as nowadays is widely used in both photovoltaic and thermal conversion. Consequently, at the Electrical Engineering Faculty of Iasi, Romania, a photovoltaic power plant of 9 kW plant was installed through the ENERED research platform project. The main goal of the project was to develop a research platform on the efficient and sustainable energy. In this paper the photovoltaic power plant will be presented along with some data regarding the electricity coverage levels while supplying several consumers with different operating regimes.

articleTitle: Using the photovoltaic renewable sources for high-voltage substation utilities
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Taking into account the fact that the photovoltaic renewable sources are spreading it is good to consider this type of source for high-voltage substation utilities. In the paper there is presented a technical solution for a photovoltaic plant created especially for the utilities of a real high-voltage substation. The results obtained show that the initial investment is covered after half of the life cycle of the solar plant.

articleTitle: Power quality system analysis on embarked systems
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The naval installation has a series of particularities compared to the industrial ones from the ground. Their dimensions are small, lightweight, should be functioning safely, efficiently at lower operating costs to enroll in the overall cost of the ship, to keep the plant competitive. A naval installation includes electronic equipment and the electrical equipment of the layout is loaded close to the maximum power. Therefore, naval equipment is a source of harmonic or inter-harmonic disturbances, which cause additional losses, unfavorable.

articleTitle: Experimental investigations of a hydroelectric power plant
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The use of renewable low power sources is currently rather reduced. Utilization of some specialized software allows the operation of the low-power hydroelectric power plants in automatic regime, without local monitoring personnel, these being able to be remotely monitored and controlled. In this way, the utilization of such low-power plants becomes profitable. The tests made at the hydroelectric power plant's commissioning have a special importance for the future operation in optimal conditions. In this work there is presented a concrete application to a hydroelectric power plant from western Romania.

articleTitle: CEUS figures finite element modelling
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: CEUS figure are actually a series of images that captures the ferrofluid spectrum movement under the action of a rotating magnetic field. Depending on the shape of the field pattern, the ferrofluid located inside a cylindrical dielectric recipient, gets a rotating movement that is highlighted by a bronze powder cluttered on the surface of it. This paper presents the results obtained from the modeling of some Grosu motor variants by the finite element modeling.

articleTitle: Typical-situations aware systems: The conceptual framework and an example of using it in the case of designing and developing a support service for experiential enriching of heritage sites
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper we give a stipulative definition of the term “situation” (a reductionist representation of the world seen as being psychological (ψ) and physical (φ) drivable) and we apply it for defining the concepts of visiting-situations tracking system (VSTS) and visiting-situations aware system (VSAS). We use these concepts to treat the hypothetical case of a HERMES service (Heritage Enriching through the Rooting Management of Experience Services) and we conceive a simple solution for designing a VSTS capable to generate the essential data for identifying the objects of a visited site and, at the same time, the attention behavior of a user-visitor regarding the respective objects.

articleTitle: Discharge simulation based on particle methods
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper is presented an discharge simulation based on particle methods. The particle-in-cell (PIC) method is a self-consistent technique in which arbitrary distribution functions of charged particles are statistically represented by discrete computer particles.

articleTitle: Energetic analysis of the subcritical low-temperature ORC by imposing the hot source outlet temperature
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The organic Rankine cycle (ORC) with subcritical pressures using the waste heat recovered from a low-temperature source was analyzed using an original assumption: to impose the hot source temperature at the outlet of the heat exchanger. This hypothesis leads to a variation of the pinch-point, when the working fluid pressure varies. For the numerical computation, a waste heat source with an inlet temperature of 150 °C and an outlet temperature of 60 °C was considered. The energetic performances of ORC were analyzed for three organic fluid types: R123, R124, and R134a.

articleTitle: Improving electromanipulation capacity of dielectrophoretic arrays based on variation of interdigitated microelectrode's geometry
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Dielectrophoresis has been proven to be a reliable method for nanoparticles manipulation and trapping at the level of interdigitated microelectrode (IDE) or as a tool to filter and characterize different nanoparticles. Within the herein paper the authors are discussing in detail the role played by the electric field gradient as a key aspect regarding the dielectrophoretic force required to trap nanoparticles. Moreover, the authors are focusing on a feasible method of manufacturing interdigitated microelectrodes that offer the possibility of fast development for laboratory grade studies and for enhancing the electrical field gradient by varying the microelectrodes' geometry and shape.

articleTitle: On the survey of the magnetic fields in power distribution substations
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper we present the results of the low frequency magnetic fields measurements inside of two transformer and distribution stations in the country of Iasi. We made measurements in different areas inside two stations, near magnetic field sources and in control rooms, by using measurement instruments, which permit both spot measurements and long term survey of magnetic fields. The highest values of the field were obtained on Section 4 of Station 1 (9845 nT) and in Station 2 near the electrical transformer (7408 nT). So, maximum values obtained in the transformer stations were under 10 μT, which means that the value of the magnetic field is less than 5% compared to the maximum allowable by ICNIRP.

articleTitle: Analysis of new formulations for nano-filled concrete, bituminous coatings and insulation
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper are presented new nano-filled materials which have been developed (Depollutant mortar, Sol-gel coating on mortar, Self-compacting concrete) and manufacture processes was studied to enhance the safety in nanomaterials.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of different means of biogas production used in cogeneration
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents a technical and economic analysis of the biogas used in cogeneration. The biogas is generated by anaerobic digestion of manure from a pig farm and a mixture of plant biomass and manure. The two solutions were economically analyzed in two scenarios of financial support schemes. The results of this study lead to the conclusion that while maintaining the support scheme based on green certificates, both cases analyzed are economically efficient.

articleTitle: The influence of the tariff charged by electricity suppliers on the optimal running of a trigeneration plant
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper shows how the use of different types of tariffs by electricity suppliers influences the optimal functioning of a trigeneration system designed to supply an electricity, heat and cold consumer.

articleTitle: Major influences in households and business spaces — Wi-Fi, telecommunication masts outputs and electrical pollution
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper offers a non-exhaustive perspective, as well as a spectrum of performed measurements, in the field of non-ionizing electromagnetic radiation. Shielding Wi-Fi is shown to be an effective means of counteracting its health risks. The effects of cell phone towers positioning next to living and working spaces is presented and analyzed. Electrical pollution mitigation is described, as well as the problem of earth bound stray electrical currents. Effective actions and measures to be taken for the benefit of future generations are suggested and justified.

articleTitle: Assessing the close field non-ionizing emissions of PC-monitors
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In recent years there has been an increase in the general concerns regarding the possible negative effects of non-ionizing electromagnetic emissions. A very common situation is determined by electric and magnetic emissions of computer monitors with which we work more than 8 hours a day. This display is located within small distance (around 50 cm) of the most sensitive organs of the human: the brain and eyes. That is the reason that the legal provisions of newly issued EU Directive 35 are completing some earlier rules, which were included in the so-called “TCO certification”. For instance, various synchronizing oscillators and switching power supply units are sources for low frequency electric and magnetic fields. It is no coincidence that the spectrum analyzer NF 5035, used by us for the measurements here reported, has preset from the design, a frequency band called TCO, a different band being dedicated to old CRT monitors and a third, to the currently all-over spread LCD monitors made in TFT technology. We have developed and applied a trustful methodology for measuring E&H field emissions of 4 types of monitors, representative for different generations. We have presented the situations when there were exceedances, issuing explanations and recommendations for control and reduction. Results and metrics were reported for cumulative, simultaneous exposure to many working displays.

articleTitle: Numerical simulations of the electromagnetic field shielding performances for reducing the induced faults in the coils of a three-phase miniature circuit breaker
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents the computer aided design (CAD) model and the computer aided engineering (CAE) simulation technologies for the analysis of the electromagnetic field shielding performances in a three phase miniature circuit breaker (MCB). The shields are used to reduce the electromagnetic field (EMF) interferences and induced current between the coils. The shielding capacity of different materials is studied, as well as the different thickness of the shielding material. A conclusion can be drawn, of what kind of material and material thickness is more suitable for this application fields.

articleTitle: Analyzing the symmetrical components of the stator current of an induction machine under internal fault
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper the symmetrical components of stator currents, if an unbalanced fault occurs in an induction machine have been analysed. A critical analysis of their expression, previously determined using the symmetrical components method, has been carried out. It was considered the impedance changing across the stator terminals as the fault effect. The analysis performed by simulation was based on studying the amplitude of two-phase stator current resulted by Park Transform.

articleTitle: Linearized model of the variable flux induction motor drive
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The advantages of the squirrel cage three-phase induction motors used in servo positioning applications are severely compromised due to the strong nonlinear coupling between the flux and the speed, which implies sophisticated control algorithms and structures. In the rotor field oriented control only an asymptotic decoupling between flux and speed / position is obtained and only if the flux is maintained at the constant value. By using the input-output linearization by state feedback, the outputs are complete decoupled. Therefore, torque optimization is possible without damaging the adjusted mechanical output variables (speed/position). In order to treats the highly nonlinear regime (working at variable flux) a powerfull tool, nonlinear multiple input - multiple output (MIMO) feedback linearization is used. In order to improve the performances of the induction machine, the obtained linearized mathematical models allow configuration of the control structures similar to the classical ones. In addition, these models can be used for the development of the optimal control of the induction machine based on the energetic criteria in the flux weakening region. The comparative numerical simulation results of the mathematical models (conventional and linearized ones) are presented in this paper. The mathematical models implemented in MATLAB-Simulink are validated during dynamic regime under the appropriate load torque step.

articleTitle: Study of TEM waves with oblique incidence at the boundary between charged, lossy dielectrics
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The TEM wave parameters in dielectrics with space charge distribution are determined analytically. The refraction on the interface between a lossy charged dielectric and a weak conductor is considered and the frequency dependence of the transmission angle, transmission and reflection coefficient are analyzed via numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Relative to the increase of electricity transmission efficiency by cables
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a new method for increasing efficiency transmission of electricity by cables, based on the change of Poynting Vector value, using an insulation electrically polarized by current conduction. The idea is to increase the tangential component of Poynting Vector, namely the density of electric power transmitted to consumers, by using special insulation of the cable which is polarized under the action of current conduction, increasing the radial component of the electric field at cable surface. The advantages of the method are: to increase the efficiency transmission of electric energy, to reduce the voltage drops, to decrease the losses due the Joule-Lenz effect, to increase the lifetime of the cable. This method is useful in the case of kilometers or tens of kilometers length of cable.

articleTitle: Numerical simulations of flow through a low head cross-flow hydro-turbine nozzle
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In many European countries a micro-hydro plant can be classified in the category renewable resource, only if it complies with environmental protection limitations. Installation of cross-flow turbines (Banki-Michell-Ossberger) require minor construction works to be done, especially for power up to 100 kW. In the case of very low heads (less than 1.5 m), sometimes is difficult to feed the turbine nozzle through a headrace pipe. In such cases it is easier to feed the nozzle directly from the existing natural water flow. This paper presents a series of numerical simulations (CFD) for several values of flow (from 100 to 200 l/s) through a low power cross-flow turbine nozzle. The analyzed flow domain corresponds to a cross-flow turbine having nozzle only on the inlet. Numerical simulations were made taking into consideration the k-epsilon turbulence model. The numerical simulations are focused on flow phenomena taking place in the nozzle of the cross-flow turbine feed directly from the water stream. The nozzle have vertical axis. A comparative analysis between the nozzle feed by a headrace pipe (through the upper section) and the nozzle feed directly from water stream (through one of his sides), is also presented. Dead zones (streamline reversal) that appear in case of the nozzle feed through one of his sides are highlighted.

articleTitle: Model identification for assisted tennis training of the sportsmen with kinetic disabilities
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper we focused on the model identification of the motion process of the tennis players with disabilities during the tennis match. An equivalent inverted pendulum model is introduced for the kinetic of the motion. The coordinates of the mass center of the body are determined by measurements with a system of video cameras and additional software. Recorded data are post-processed by means of a dedicated software. The aim of the work was to assist the sportsman and his trainer, and to improve the safety of the sportsman during the game.

articleTitle: A solution for study of positioning control of two axes
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: For engineering students, it is very important that the laboratory work should be more practical, in order to provide an experience closer to the real world applications. In this paper, a solution to study the positioning control of two axes is presented. The solution is made with a PLC, two kind of HMI, a drive capable to manage two axes with high performance positioning, an induction motor and a brushless motor. The industrial communications used in this application are ProfiNET and ProfiBUS. The proposed solution can be used by the students to develop software applications, from low to high complexity.

articleTitle: Continuous direct torque versus predictive control of the induction motor
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: For electric traction applications based on induction motor, the preferred technique for control is the direct torque one (DTC). It has advantages, as it is a sensorless control technique, but also disadvantages. The main disadvantage is related to the switching frequency which is the same with the sampling frequency of the entire control loop. This determines high requirements for the control system which must be quite performant. In order to avoid this disadvantage, the classical hysteresis controllers are replaced by continuous ones which ensures the decoupling of the pulses width by the control sampling period. The controls are simulated for different values of the fixed step. The results are then evaluated face to the ones obtained when the predictive concepts are used for obtaining the pulse width modulation strategy of a voltage fed inverter which supplies an induction motor, as the both determine, during each sampling period, the next stator voltage phasor, but considering different criteria. The reference values of the currents are obtained from a classical rotor flux vector control scheme. The described technique is similar with the preset currents (bang-bang) pulse width modulation technique, but it has the advantage of fixed switching frequency.

articleTitle: Operating regime efficiency analysis of a small photovoltaic power plant
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Solar energy represents one of the most promising renewable resource, being widely exploited nowadays. Both, thermal and photovoltaic conversion installations are now used from small domestic applications to large power plants. At the Electrical Engineering Faculty of Iasi, Romania, a small 4.32 kW, photovoltaic power plant was installed, for didactical purposes and also energy production, as is supplying several consumers from the Power Engineering Departments building. In this paper the photovoltaic power plant will be presented along with some data regarding the electricity coverage level while supplying several consumers with different operating regimes.

articleTitle: The control system modeling of winder with hybrid Fuzzy-PID controller
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper trying to present design a hybrid Fuzzy-PID controller, to increase the performance of the winder for high speed wire drawing machine. The hybrid Fuzzy-PID controller was designed used as a basis fuzzy logic and mathematical model of the PID controller. Data for estimation of the model are taken from a real winder mechanism of wire drawing machine. For hybrid structure of the PID controller parameter estimation are used Fuzzy logic. Through Math Lab modeling we have choose fuzzy rules that are meant to count the parameters of the PID controller. The winder's performance has improved meaningfully, if make a compare with conventional Fuzzy controller.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Luz Flat Tracker power plants
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical and Power Engineering (EPE)
